meta.label: Language learning
meta.attribution: Drawn from platform terms of use, refund and satisfaction-guarantee pages, published prices and app-store listings, tutor pay and commission pages, government pages on free adult English classes, nonprofit tax records and public-domain course archives, not audited by us. Language apps mostly teach vocabulary and grammar through repetition; live tutoring and structured audio courses cost more but put a person, not a streak counter, in charge of your progress. Where a platform's own pages could not be read directly, the score is left out rather than guessed. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare language learning by teaching quality, cost, buyer protection, and labor practices.

axes.label: Cost or overall fit
axes.question: Lower cost or a stronger overall fit?

axes.label: Buyer protection
axes.question: Do you want the seller to carry the loss?

criteria.label: Teaching quality (structured, human-led teaching over solo drilling)
Refund or recourse if it does not work for you
Whether the tutor keeps most of what you pay

products.name: Duolingo
products.description: A free, gamified vocabulary and grammar app with a paid Super tier that removes ads, hearts and lesson limits.

economical.note: Duolingo's own App Store listing shows Super Duolingo subscription tiers priced from $9.99 to $12.99 a month or roughly $84 to $120 a year, on top of a free tier that remains usable without payment.

labor.note: Duolingo has no tutors to pay; the people behind its lessons are staff and contractors. In the all-hands memo Duolingo published on its own LinkedIn page in April 2025 (the memo text is in the image attached to the post), CEO Luis von Ahn said the company is going to be AI-first, that it had replaced a slow, manual content creation process with one powered by AI, that 'We’ll gradually stop using contractors to do work that AI can handle', and that headcount will only be given if a team cannot automate more of its work. His May 2025 follow-up post said he does not see AI as replacing what Duolingo's employees do and that it is continuing to hire at the same speed, but it did not withdraw the contractor policy, so little of what you pay is committed to human course creators.

products.name: Babbel
products.description: A subscription app of short structured lessons built around everyday conversation topics, with a legally required EU-style withdrawal window rather than a marketing money-back guarantee.

buyer_protection.note: Babbel's own End User Terms state you have the right to withdraw from the contract within 14 days without giving a reason and be reimbursed all payments, but that if you cancel a subscription to join a Group Plan no refund is issued, including for any unused portion.

products.name: Rosetta Stone
products.description: A long-running immersion-method app with per-language and unlimited-language subscription tiers, plus a one-time purchase option and a 30-day money-back guarantee on direct purchases.

economical.note: Rosetta Stone's own App Store listing lists a 1-year unlimited-languages subscription at $109.99, 12 months of a single language at $109.99 to $119.99, 3-month single-language plans around $44.99 to $54.99, and a one-time 5-level single-language purchase at $199.99.

buyer_protection.note: Rosetta Stone's own support page states Classic subscriptions purchased from its website come with a 30-day, no-risk, money-back guarantee, which applies only to purchases made directly from Rosetta Stone and not to purchases made through third-party retailers such as the Apple App Store or Google Play.

products.name: Busuu
products.description: A CEFR-levelled course app now owned by Chegg, with a 14-day cancellation right that still charges for the value of any lessons already used.

buyer_protection.note: Busuu's own Terms of Service say you may cancel a Premium Service purchase and claim a refund for any reason within 14 days of the contract being formed, but that if you have used the Premium Service before cancelling you must pay for the value of the service already provided up to the cancellation date.

products.name: Pimsleur
products.description: An audio-only course built on Dr. Paul Pimsleur's research into aural recall, using 30-minute listen-and-repeat lessons without transcripts, sold as a subscription with a 30-day money-back guarantee on direct purchases.

educational.note: Pimsleur's own FAQ describes the method as built on Dr. Pimsleur's research finding that the fastest way to learn a language was by listening to and recalling new words or phrases from memory, deliberately without transcripts or note-taking, because learners who tried to write during lessons were found to recall less and use the language less fluently in conversation.

buyer_protection.note: Pimsleur's own satisfaction guarantee page offers a 30-day money-back guarantee for subscriptions purchased directly from Pimsleur.com, but excludes gift subscriptions, subscriptions with a free trial of 7 days or longer, and purchases made through Apple or Google in-app billing.

products.name: Lingoda
products.description: A subscription of live small-group classes with real teachers, priced per month by how many classes you take, including a fixed-term Sprint plan that pays back part of the cost if you finish it.

buyer_protection.note: Lingoda's own FAQ states new subscribers can cancel a monthly plan at any time so it will not renew, and that a Sprint plan down payment can only be refunded if you cancel within 14 days of signing up.

products.name: italki
products.description: A marketplace of live 1:1 lessons where tutors set their own hourly rate, with a Professional Teacher track for formally qualified instructors and a cheaper Community Tutor track for informal conversation practice.

educational.note: italki's own pricing guide describes Professional Teachers as having formal teaching qualifications, language certifications or structured lesson plans and typically charging $10 to $40 a lesson, while Community Tutors are native or fluent speakers without formal teacher training who typically charge $4 to $20 a lesson for conversation practice.

labor.note: italki's own pricing guide states italki takes a commission from the teacher's side of the transaction and that students pay only the lesson price shown on the teacher's profile with no added booking fee, meaning tutors set their own rate but the platform's cut is taken out of what the tutor receives rather than added on top for the student.

products.name: Preply
products.description: A marketplace of live 1:1 tutoring similar to italki, where the platform's commission is highest for new tutors and falls the more hours a tutor teaches.

labor.note: Preply's own Help Center article on its commission model states the commission is 100 percent on every new student's trial lesson, starts at 33 percent for new tutors, and falls to 28 percent after 20 hours taught and eventually to 18 percent for tutors with more than 400 hours taught.

products.name: HelloTalk
products.description: A free peer-to-peer language exchange app where you practice with native speakers of your target language in exchange for helping them practice yours, with an optional paid VIP tier for extra tools.

economical.note: HelloTalk's own blog describes its core features, including text, voice and video exchange with language partners, as free, with a VIP tier that unlocks extras such as ad removal and additional AI tools.

educational.note: HelloTalk's own blog describes its Language Exchange feature as a mutual, unstructured arrangement where no payment changes hands and each partner practices their target language for an equal amount of time, rather than a designed curriculum taught by a qualified teacher.

products.name: Foreign Service Institute courses (via Live Lingua)
products.brand: US Department of State / Live Lingua
products.description: Free public-domain language courses originally built by the US government to train diplomats, now hosted for free download by the nonprofit-style Live Lingua Project; the material is thorough but decades old in places and comes with no live teacher.

economical.note: US law, 17 U.S.C. section 105, states that copyright protection is not available for any work of the United States Government, which is the legal basis for the Foreign Service Institute's original course materials being public domain and free to copy; the Live Lingua Project's own page says it hosts over 127 FSI courses, 161 ebooks and 4,169 audio files at no cost.

educational.note: The Live Lingua Project's own page for the FSI courses says the original files were produced by the US Foreign Service Institute and states it hosts over 127 courses across more than 40 languages, each including recorded audio drills alongside written material, though the courses are self-directed with no live teacher or feedback.

products.name: Anki
products.description: A free, open-source spaced-repetition flashcard program used widely for vocabulary memorization; it is a study tool rather than a course, so you supply or download your own decks.

economical.note: Harvey Mudd College's Computing and Information Services describes Anki as a free, open source application for creating flashcards, and Anki's own website confirms the desktop version is free on all major platforms with only the official iPhone app sold as a paid one-time purchase.

educational.note: Anki's own website frames it as a spaced-repetition flashcard program that anyone can extend through add-ons, with no built-in language curriculum of its own; the learner has to build or download a deck rather than follow a designed course.

products.name: LingQ
products.description: A reading- and listening-based app built around imported and native-speaker content that you look up word by word, sold as a monthly Premium membership with a first-time 30-day refund window.

buyer_protection.note: LingQ's own Terms of Service state that if you initially signed up for a Premium account and are not satisfied at any time during the first 30 days you are entitled to a full refund of your membership fee, but that the service is otherwise non-refundable with no credit for partial or unused months.

products.name: Free through your public library
products.description: Many public libraries pay for patrons to use a course library such as Mango Languages at no cost with just a library card, covering dozens of languages plus English-learning courses.

economical.note: The Los Angeles Public Library's own Mango Languages page states the service is free, online language learning in languages that include Spanish, French, Italian, Chinese, Arabic, Korean, Russian and more, and requires only an LAPL library card to access.

products.name: Memrise
products.description: A vocabulary and phrase app built around short clips of native speakers, with a limited free plan and a Pro subscription that unlocks all lessons, videos and unlimited speaking practice.

economical.note: Memrise's own App Store listing describes the free plan as limited (limited vocab lessons, limited videos and conversations, with ads) and lists in-app subscription prices including a Monthly plan at $24.99, an Annual plan at $61.99 and a Lifetime plan at $329.99, so the free tier is a taster rather than a full course.

buyer_protection.note: Memrise's own Terms of Use state 'We offer a 30-day money-back guarantee' for a full refund on Quarterly or Annual plans if you are not satisfied, and separately give every plan, including Monthly, a 14-day right to cancel for a refund under the UK Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013; refunds do not apply to renewals or to Apple App Store payments, which must be claimed from the store.

products.name: Mondly
products.description: A gamified app covering 41 languages with chatbot and speech-recognition practice, owned by the education publisher Pearson, with a limited free tier and a Premium subscription.

economical.note: Mondly's own App Store listing says you can learn 41 languages for free and lists Premium subscription prices of $15.90 a month or $74.90 for 12 months of unlimited access, with discounted offers such as a monthly plan at $7.99.

buyer_protection.note: Mondly's own Subscription Terms state 'All amounts are non-refundable unless otherwise stated in these Subscription Terms', and grant a full refund on direct purchases only to subscribers in the UK or EU, within 14 days of the subscription starting, a trial ending or a renewal; App Store and Google Play purchases must be refunded by the store, and partially used subscriptions are otherwise not refunded.

products.name: Drops
products.description: A visual vocabulary game for more than 55 languages, played in short timed sessions, with a free tier and a Premium subscription that removes the time limit and ads.

economical.note: Drops' own App Store listing says over 50 million people use Drops for free language lessons and lists Premium in-app prices ranging from $7.99 to $99.99; the free tier is time-limited, with Premium unlocking unlimited time per Drops' own website.

buyer_protection.note: Drops' own Terms and Conditions state 'We do not provide refunds after 14 days of the original purchase', that it does not refund Apple App Store payments because Apple manages them, and that it offers no refunds or partial refunds outside those terms, including for time left when you delete your account.

products.name: Clozemaster
products.description: A fill-in-the-gap sentence game for intermediate learners that drills vocabulary in context across many languages, free to play with an optional Pro subscription.

economical.note: Clozemaster's own Pro page lists Pro at $12.99 a month or $79.99 a year, and its homepage says the game is free to play, with Pro unlocking advanced features for power users rather than gating the core sentence practice.

buyer_protection.note: Clozemaster's own Pro page says the Yearly plan has a 30-day money-back guarantee if you email to cancel, but 'No refunds will be issued after 30 days, no refunds for Monthly plans'; its Terms add that the 30-day refund applies to yearly subscriptions purchased via the website.

products.name: Tandem
products.description: A free language exchange app that pairs you with native speakers who want to learn your language, with an optional Tandem Pro subscription for extra tools.

economical.note: Tandem's own App Store listing says many features are free and that Tandem Pro is an optional subscription for access to all features, with in-app Tandem Pro prices listed from $14.99 to $80.00.

educational.note: Tandem's own homepage describes the service as a language exchange where two members help each other with their target languages (one partner helps with German while the other helps with English), which is peer practice with no designed curriculum or qualified teacher, the same model as HelloTalk.

buyer_protection.note: Tandem's own Terms of Service give consumers the right to withdraw from the contract within 14 days without giving any reason and be reimbursed all payments, but state that App Store and Google Play purchases are subject to those stores' policies, which may not provide refunds, and that purchases are otherwise final.

products.name: Glossika
products.description: A sentence-repetition speaking trainer built on native-speaker audio in 50-plus languages, sold as a single-language or all-languages subscription, with some minority languages free.

economical.note: Glossika's own App Store listing lists Glossika Plus (one language) at $19.99 a month or $129.99 a year and Glossika Pro (all languages) at $39.99 a month or $299.99 a year after a free trial; its homepage marks a handful of languages, such as Catalan, Scottish Gaelic, Welsh and Manx, as free.

buyer_protection.note: Glossika's own Terms and Conditions state that for monthly plans 'Subscriptions for the current month are final', while annual subscribers may downgrade or cancel within 60 days of payment to receive a refund on the remaining amount; its free trial needs no card and does not convert to a charge automatically.

products.name: Speechling
products.description: A nonprofit pronunciation-coaching service where you record sentences and get feedback from human coaches, free up to a monthly allowance with a paid unlimited plan and scholarships for those who cannot pay.

economical.note: Speechling's own pricing page offers a Forever Free plan with the whole curriculum and up to 10 coaching sessions a month (except in English, French, Chinese and German), and Speechling Unlimited from $19.99 a month; its mission page says it is a nonprofit that charges just enough to cover coaching costs and gives full scholarships to those who cannot afford it, and ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer lists it as a 501(c)(3) organisation.

educational.note: Speechling's own mission page describes its method as spaced-repetition sentence practice combined with human coaching, with certified pronunciation coaches giving feedback on your recorded speaking similar to a private tutor; it is narrowly focused on speaking and pronunciation rather than a full course with a teacher.

products.name: Cambly
products.description: An English-only conversation platform with native-speaking tutors on demand, sold as monthly plans for small-group, private or structured Pro lessons, with tutors paid a fixed per-minute rate set by Cambly.

economical.note: Cambly's own website lists plans starting from $17 a month for small groups, $39 a month for Private+ one-on-one lessons and $56 a month for Pro (discounted from $24, $56 and $80), and says you can explore without a subscription; regular live lessons cost far more a year than an app.

educational.note: Cambly's own website describes live conversations with native English speakers, lesson recordings and transcripts, automated feedback, and a Pro tier with exclusive tutors and structured, goal-oriented lessons; it advertises tutors as native speakers rather than requiring a teaching qualification, so it scores below italki's qualified-teacher track.

labor.note: Cambly's own tutor recruitment page says 'You make $0.17/min ($10.2/hour) on Cambly' and $0.20 a minute ($12 an hour) on Cambly Kids, paid weekly; tutors are paid this flat rate set by Cambly rather than setting their own prices as on italki or Preply, and Cambly does not publish what share of a student's plan price that represents.

products.name: Verbling
products.description: A marketplace of 1:1 video lessons with teachers who must show prior teaching experience, where teachers set their own hourly rates and refunds come only as site credit.

economical.note: Verbling's own homepage lists lessons from $7 an hour for French and $8 for Spanish up to $15 for English and $18 for Japanese or Korean, with a free trial lesson; a weekly lesson adds up to several hundred dollars a year.

educational.note: Verbling's own teacher application page says all teachers must have previous experience teaching their language to speakers of other languages, that a formal teaching certificate is preferred, that candidates without a certificate or verifiable experience are not accepted, and that teachers need C2 command of the language they teach.

buyer_protection.note: Verbling's own Terms of Use say there are no refunds for cancelling an account, that 'All purchases at Verbling are final and cannot be refunded to the original form of payment', and that purchased classes can only be cancelled and refunded as Verbling credit.

products.name: Language Transfer
products.description: Free, donation-funded audio courses using 'The Thinking Method', with complete courses in Spanish, Greek and Swahili and introductions to several more languages.

economical.note: Language Transfer's App Store listing shows the app as free with free audio courses, and the project's own About page says everything is free, that it is sustained by learner donations and that donations do not unlock any extra material.

educational.note: Language Transfer's own FAQ says its Complete courses explore the entire structural panorama of the language and build vocabulary, while Introduction courses cover roughly the first 30 to 40 percent; the courses are audio-only and designed to make you an independent learner, with no live teacher or feedback, much like Pimsleur's structured audio approach.

products.name: ESOL classes at a college or adult education centre (England)
products.description: English for Speakers of Other Languages courses run in person by further education colleges, adult education centres and community venues; for learning English only, and usually free or discounted for adults in England.

economical.note: GOV.UK says adults over 16 who have left school can take English for speakers of other languages (ESOL) courses, which 'are also normally discounted or free depending on your employment status and how long you have been resident in England', and that Learner Support may help if there is a fee.

educational.note: GOV.UK lists ESOL as a course you take at further education colleges, adult education centres, some libraries, children's centres and other community venues, meaning an in-person course run by an education provider rather than solo app drilling; it does not publish teacher qualification requirements, so it scores just below italki's qualified-teacher track.

products.name: USA Learns
products.description: Free online English and US citizenship courses for adults, made by a California public education agency and pointed to by the US government's own Learn English page.

economical.note: USAGov's Learn English page says you can find free and low-cost classes to learn English as a Second Language and points to USALearns.org for online videos and lessons; USA Learns' own homepage says its English classes and its Citizenship course are free, though the site carries advertisements.

educational.note: USA Learns' own homepage describes sequenced English courses (a 1st and 2nd English course plus reading and citizenship practice) with lessons covering speaking, vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, listening, reading and writing, and lets teachers create classes and enrol students; used alone it is self-study with no live teacher.
